title: Tenant epoch lattice, safe reset probe, and post-reset reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We have recurring anomalies when monthly/daily quota resets happen for customers on Reserved Capacity and cross-region deployments. Symptoms include double-applied resets after leader failover, transient overdraw where a tenant briefly exceeds their carved pool, and noisy billing reconciliation runs that require manual adjustments. Root causes traced to (1) synchronous hard resets that ignore in-flight deltas and eventual leader re-election, (2) per-region reset timing skew for tenants with multi-region presence, and (3) lack of a pre-reset verification step to guarantee idempotent application of the reset in our ledger.

Goal: Implement a robust, observable reset mechanism for tenant quota epochs that: (a) reduces harmful reset-induced drift, (b) is safe across leader changes and retries, (c) supports variable granularity (hourly/daily/monthly anchors) for reserved and hosted customers, and (d) emits explicit reconciliation artifacts for billing.

Proposed approach (overview):
1) Epoch lattice: instead of a single rigid reset anchor, represent tenant quota epochs as a small lattice of overlapping anchors (anchor primary = billing anchor e.g., tenant billing_day; anchor secondary = sliding window offsets e.g., tenant-local-midnight/region). The lattice gives us tolerance for timezone/dst and region skew.
2) Safe reset probe: a three-phase reset protocol for each tenant epoch:
   - Probe: read last-commit timestamp, active lease holder, and in-flight delta buffer size. If probe observes a concurrent reset or active in-flight write above tolerance, delay or schedule retry.
   - Pre-commit snapshot: capture a compact delta (usage_delta) against the current ledger and persist a tombstone/reset-intent record in the reset-log with a monotonic reset_id. This makes the reset discoverable and idempotent.
   - Commit: atomically apply the reset using a compare-and-swap on ledger epoch markers (or via an append-only event for ledger-based stores). Emit an audit event and compact reconciliation work item.
3) Post-reset reconciliation: after commit, enqueue a reconciliation job that verifies the tenant's effective available units vs expected outcome. If drift > threshold (configurable, default 0.5%), create a reconciliation adjustment event (for visibility and billing pipeline) and, for reserved pools, attempt a bounded corrective transfer from the tenant's burst buffer rather than immediate billing credits.
4) Cross-region ordering: when tenant data exists in multiple regions, reset jobs should pick a region-priority order using tenant metadata (primary region first). Use short-lived cross-region leases to avoid duplicate commits; timeouts degrade to 'snapshot-merge' mode.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- Consistency vs latency: The probe/snapshot steps add small latency to resets but prevent costly manual reconciliations. We limit probe windows to 3s by default and favor retries over blocking production traffic.
- Complexity: introduces reset-log and reconciliation queue. To manage complexity, reuse existing lease/leader primitives and the reconciliation worker framework.
- Observability: each reset must emit structured telemetry: reset_id, tenant, anchor_type, probe_result, precommit_delta, commit_latency, reconciliation_outcome. These must be captured at token-level for billing traces.
- Backwards compatibility: Provide a feature flag gated rollout per-tenant; legacy instant reset path remains until full validation is complete.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
- Automated unit + integration tests covering leader failover during each phase (probe/precommit/commit).
- E2E test demonstrating no double-apply after simulated leader flapping and that post-reset reconciliation produces audit event when drift > threshold.
- Benchmarks showing median reset latency under 250ms (excluding reconciliation job) at 1000 tenant resets/sec synthetic load.
- Telemetry: dashboards for reset attempt rate, probe pass/fail, median commit latency, reconciliation adjustment count and total adjusted units; alerts for >0.1% failed reconciliations in production.
- Migration/rollout plan documented in the ticket and implementation PR, including feature-flag gating, 1%/10%/100% ramp, and rollback instructions.

Notes on quota semantics: Reserved pools allow tenants to borrow within pool limits. The reconciliation phase must attempt intra-pool smoothing first (transfer from tenant's pool carry buffer) before creating a billing adjustment. This preserves SLAs and minimizes customer-facing charge churn.

Operational runbook pointers:
- If reconciliation job shows persistent drift > 2% for a tenant after 3 attempts, escalate to billing-owner and create INC-BILL-XXXX.
- To force a manual reset for a tenant, use the admin-reset command which writes a reset-intent and runs the precommit/commit path; admin actions must include reason and operator id to satisfy audit logs.

Deliverables:
- Service changes: quota-reset service updates, reset-log schema migration, reconciliation worker extension.
- Console changes: new reset audit view and tenant-level reset timeline (UI work tracked separately).
- PRs: implementation, migration, and tests.

Release plan: feature-flagged in reservations-2026.03, beta to Reserved customers on March 25, 2026, full ramp after 2 weeks of monitoring and no >0.1% reconciliation failures.
comments: 2026-03-03 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial triage. Captured recurring incidents where resets overlapped with leader failovers. P0 for correctness, recommended P1 for delivery due to complexity.

2026-03-05 - Marco Alvarez: Spike completed. Verified that our current reset path lacks a persistent reset-intent; drafted three-phase protocol. Identified required reset-log schema changes and small migration. Estimated 5 points.

2026-03-07 - Design review (Diane Chu): Reviewed epoch lattice idea. Agreed this helps DST and cross-region skew. Recommended adding explicit per-tenant region-priority metadata and keeping probe timeout configurable via feature flag.

2026-03-09 - Engineering note: Implemented reset-log schema v1 with fields (reset_id, tenant, anchor_type, precommit_delta, status, created_at, operator). Migration script ready in branch feature/ENG-112358/reset-log-migration.

2026-03-11 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/quota-service/pull/2146 - implements probe + precommit snapshot and writes reset-intent. Needs reviewers @sneha, @tj. CI failing on integration test that simulates leader switchover.
2026-03-12 - QA: Integration test updated to wait for quorum; reproduces double-apply prior to fix. Added test case for cross-region snapshot-merge. Marked flaky test for follow-up (ENG-112359).

2026-03-13 - Marco Alvarez: Fixed race by extending precommit CAS to include leader-epoch; re-ran CI, all tests passing. Added metric reset_commit_latency_ms and probe_failures_total. Preparing rollout doc.

2026-03-14 - Rollout plan draft: 1% tenants (non-critical) behind flag for 48 hours, collect metrics; then 10% for 1 week; verify reconciliation failures <0.1% and median commit latency within target before wider ramp. Rollback: flip feature flag off; reconciliation worker will continue to process pending jobs in legacy mode.
